- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 5–10 days.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.7); apply +1.5% bias to first 7 days.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.8 to -0.5), model lags; adjust forecast to match sentiment shift within 2–3 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30-day forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 2–5% for next 7 days unless sentiment supports continuation.
- In high-sentiment periods (e.g., 0.6–0.8), model often overfits short-term volatility; smooth 30d forecast by averaging with 18d moving average for next 5 days.
